sentences.text: JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that the deceased was an agricultural labourer under the respondent No.1 in his Tractor and trailer bearing Reg.No.AP- 04-BK-2372 and AP-04-BK-2373.
The respondent No.1 constructing an agricultural shed at his village.
That on 06.09.2023 the respondent No.1 sent his tractor and trailer to fetch a stone gravel along with deceased for loading and unloading with the driver for his agricultural shed.
After loaded the stone gravel at crusher the driver stopped the tractor and trailer at Mudindalapalli village at about 12.00 p.m, by allowing deceased to get into the trailer for unloading the same.

When the deceased was boarding into the trailer, the driver moved the tractor and trailer at high speed in rash and negligent manner, in the result the deceased fell down, the Trailer Tyre ran over him and caused grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Prashanti Hospital, Rayachoty and after first aid he was referred to RIMS Hospital, Kadapa.
Wherein during the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
It is alleged that the accident occurred due to carelessness, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor and trailer.
Hence the jurisdictional police registered a case against the driver of said Tractor in Crime No.83/2023 for the offences punishable u/s 304(A) of IPC and also filed charge sheet against him.
The first respondent being the owner of the Tractor and trailer and second respondent being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Inspite of due service of the notice of petition, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 filed objections statement admitting the issuance of Liability Only Policy in respect of Tractor & Trailer bearing Reg.No.AP-04-BK-2372 and AP-04- BK-2373.

Further this respondent contended that it has issued statutory policy and not collected any premium under IMT-70 for covering risk of coolies / occupants carried in Tractor and Trailer and policy does not cover the risk of coolies except driver.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of section 134(c) of IMV Act is pleaded.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured Tractor & Trailer did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

sentences.text: Further it is denied the relationship of the deceased with the petitioners and also denied the employee and employer relationship of the deceased with the respondent No.1 and the accident during the course of employment and also coverage of coolie under the policy.
As per the Certificate of Registration Form-23, seating capacity is only one i.e., driver.
Further it is denied that the deceased was the earning person as he was aged 17 years as on the date of death.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 06.09.2023 at about 12.00 noon,
at Mudindlapalli village, Galidveedu mandal, Annammayya District, Andhra Pradesh,
due to actionable negligence of the driver of Tractor-Trailer, bearing Reg.No.AP-04-BK-2372 & AP-04-BK-2373 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. The Petitioner No.2 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 10 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The petitioners have also examined eye-witness to the accident as PW.2 and got marked his Aadhar card as per Ex.P.11.
In order to prove its defence, the respondent No.1 examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1.
Ex's.R1 to 4 were marked on behalf of the insurance company.
7. Arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following :

sentences.text: During the course of investigation, material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them.
Spot sketch corroborate the place of accident.
From the inquest and the postmortem report it is evident that the deceased succumbed to the fatal injuries suffered in a Road Traffic Accident.
The IMV report goes to show that at the time of inspection the vehicle involved in the accident and no damages were found.
Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested the vehicle and thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles.
Therefore the driver of Tractor and Trailer did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
The fact that yet he drove the said vehicle with high speed rashly and negligently and caused the accident.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section 304A of IPC and 184 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
9. Moreover the respondent No.2 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of Tractor and Trailer, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of driver of said vehicle is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of Tractor and Trailer has to be disbelieved.
But in the instant case, for the best reasons known to him the owner of the offending vehicle did not appeared before the court and he was been placed exparte.
As such, an adverse inference is drawn against him accordingly.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the Tractor and trailer bearing Reg.No.AP-04-BK-2372 and AP-04-BK-2373.
As such, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE No.1 :The petitioner No.2 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed that she is the mother and petitioner No.1 is the father of the deceased.
The documents i.e., Ex.P8 to 10 notarized copies of the Aadhaar cards of the petitioners and deceased placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE No.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- due to the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.

It is the specific defence urged by the petitioners counsel that the deceased was aged about 18 years and was working as a agricultural coolie under 1st respondent and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to the accidental death the petitioners were put into great mental shock and agony.
The respondent No.2 denied the age and working as coolie and not an earning member of the family and he was depending on the income of the parents / petitioners.

sentences.text: " 10. Admittedly, the deceased was aged 17 years as on the date of the accident.
He might not be an adult but he cannot be considered as a child.
He has to be considered as an adolescent.

Section 2(i) and (ii) of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (for short "the Act") defines as follows :
"(i) "adolescent" means a person who has completed his fourteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year;
"(ii) "Child" means a person who has not completed his fourteenth year of age or such age as may be specified in the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (35 of 2009), whichever is more."
11. Section 3 of the Act prohibits employment of a child in certain occupations and processes. The said Act does not prohibit the adolescent of 17 years to involve in a milk vending business.

sentences.text: The deceased and his family are from rural area and it is common for a person of 17 years to be involved in milk vending or similar occupations.
The Tribunal has completely lost sight of this fact and the reasoning is contrary to and in the teeth of the statutory provisions.

12. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 while determining the multiplier / multiplicand in accidental claims, has taken into consideration persons from the age group of 15 years and onwards while fixing the multiplier.

The erudite judgment has not only stood the test of reason but has also stood the test of time.

In fact, the Constitutional Bench of the Apex Court, has approved and upheld the methodology settled in Sarla Verma's case to calculate the multiplier /
multiplicand.

The reasoning of the Tribunal, virtually renders etiose the methodology settled in Sarla Verma's case and approved by the Constitutional Bench in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., V. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

The said ratio cannot be applied to the case of an adolescent who is 15 years and above."
Relying upon the ratio laid down in the decision supra, this Court has to consider the income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Hence the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m, as the accident took place in the year 2023.
Needless to mention, also taking into consideration the age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the present cost of living.

13. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P8, wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.01.2007, which indicates that he was aged (16 years 8 months 5 days) 17 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '18'.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 17 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased was aged about 17 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e., 40%).

Further as stated above that, deceased was a bachelor

, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenditure.

On such deduction,
the income of the deceased comes to Rs.11,200/- p.m. (Rs.22,400/- X 50/100).
16. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,200/- p.m. and the multiplier "18" is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.24,19,200/- (Rs.11,200 X 12 X 18)
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.24,19,200/- under the head of loss of dependency.

17. In this case, petitioner No.1 & 2 are the father and mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a daughter causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
The plea of insurance company is that as per the terms and conditions of the policy, the risk of the coolies is not covered.
As such there is no liability on its part to pay compensation.

20. Admittedly the offending vehicle is a Tractor and trailer and it should be considered as Open /
Misc and Special Type of Vehicle.

The contents of complaint lodged (the basis for FIR and consequently charge sheet) make it amply clear that on the fateful day of the occurrence of the accident the deceased was traveling in the offending Tractor and trailer as a coolie engaged by the insured.
No doubt the policy issued by the respondent No.2 is a Liability Only policy.

The learned advocate for respondent argued that if deceased is considered as coolie, the insurance company has no liability to pay the compensation as it is only liability only policy and if third party other than inmates injured or died, then only the company is liable.
In the present case, the owner has not paid additional premium to cover the risk of coolies.
If the deceased is considered as inmate also the respondent No.2 company has not liable to pay the compensation as inmate is not covered as a third party.

In this regard he relied on the decision reported in ILR 2017 KAR 2749 (Dharwad Bench) in the case of K. Koushik V/s Sri. Sandeep and others, wherein it is held that :
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Section 163A- Accident claim filed by the son of het deceased - Judgment and Award - Insurer's appeal challenging the liability fastened on it- Claimant's appeal for ehnahcement - Deceased was traveling as an occupant in a private car - Whether the occupant / inmate of a private car is a third party and the risk of the said third party is covered under the insurance policy ?- HELD, the occupants / passengers / inmates of a private vehicle do not fall within the definition of the word 'Third party' - The occupant / inmate of a private car is not a third party.

sentences.text: - The additional premium paid at Rs.800/- to cover the risk of the third parties cannot be held to cover the risk of inmates / occupants.
It is not a case of additional premium being collected to cover the risk of inmates along with third parties.
It is only in a contractual liability, the risk of the inmates / occupants of the private car are covered.

- The impugned judgment and order is modified absolving the insurance company from the liability and fastening the liability on the registered owner of the vehicle / respondent No.2.

In the said decision Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held as under :
Deceased along with others was traveling in truck and during the journey he got down from truck to answer the call of nature and when he was trying to board the truck, driver suddenly moved the truck due to which he fell down and sustained fatal injuries -
Tribunal fastened liability on the insurance company -
Insurance company disputes its liability on the ground that deceased was a gratuitous passenger in goods vehicle -

Deceased traveled in the truck as gratuitous passenger but he met with accident after getting down from truck and while trying to board the truck therefore deceased cannot be considered a passenger in the goods vehicle but he was a third party -

Whether Tribunal was justified in holding insurance company liable - Held:
yes.
23.

In view of the above decision the third party is the deceased who is obviously not within the vehicle either as a driver or an employee traveling in the vehicle or even as a passenger and in any way connected to the vehicle and in that connection traveling in the vehicle and so permitted by the provisions of the Act.
The decisions relied by the respondent the facts of the case and present case are very different.
But the decision relied by the petitioners is aptly applicable to the present case.
In view of the above decision, though the deceased was traveling in the Tractor at the time of incident he was not in the tractor.
As per the charge sheet came to tractor boarding into the tractor at Echi between the tractor engine and traveller.
Meantime the accused suddenly moved the tractor once with negligent manner with high speed.

Then the deceased loosed his control and fell down on the road, at that time the rear tyre of the tractor Trolley climbed over the deceased with result of it,
deceased sustained grievous injuries and died at hospital.
It clears that the deceased was neither coolie nor inmate of the tractor, he was third party.
When he came to Echi accident took place due to the negligence of driver.
Hence he is considered as third party and the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Tractor and Trailer and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount together with interest within two months from the date of this Siddayya N Alias Nachukkuri Siddayya vs Krishnareddy Alias Cheepathi ... on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131364038/

24. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988 is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,35,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 : 30%
 Petitioner No.2 : 70%
 Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
The respondent No.1 constructing an agricultural shed at his village.
After loaded the stone gravel at crusher the driver stopped the tractor and trailer at Mudindalapalli village at about 12.00 p.m, by allowing deceased to get into the trailer for unloading the same.
When the deceased was boarding into the trailer, the driver moved the tractor and trailer at high speed in rash and negligent manner, in the result the deceased fell down, the Trailer Tyre ran over him and caused grievous injuries.
Wherein during the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries.
Hence the jurisdictional police registered a case against the driver of said Tractor in Crime No.83/2023 for the offences punishable u/s 304(A) of IPC and also filed charge sheet against him.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 06.09.2023 at about 12.00 noon,
at Mudindlapalli village, Galidveedu mandal, Annammayya District, Andhra Pradesh,
due to actionable negligence of the driver of Tractor-Trailer, bearing Reg.No.AP-04-BK-2372 & AP-04-BK-2373 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore the driver of Tractor and Trailer did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
The fact that yet he drove the said vehicle with high speed rashly and negligently and caused the accident.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section 304A of IPC and 184 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
9. Moreover the respondent No.2 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of Tractor and Trailer, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of driver of said vehicle is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.
The deceased and his family are from rural area and it is common for a person of 17 years to be involved in milk vending or similar occupations.
12. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 while determining the multiplier / multiplicand in accidental claims, has taken into consideration persons from the age group of 15 years and onwards while fixing the multiplier.
The Tribunal has relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Kishan Gopal and another V. Lala and Others reported in AIR 2013 SC 5037.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 17 years.
The plea of insurance company is that as per the terms and conditions of the policy, the risk of the coolies is not covered.
20. Admittedly the offending vehicle is a Tractor and trailer and it should be considered as Open /
Misc and Special Type of Vehicle.
The contents of complaint lodged (the basis for FIR and consequently charge sheet) make it amply clear that on the fateful day of the occurrence of the accident the deceased was traveling in the offending Tractor and trailer as a coolie engaged by the insured.
If the deceased is considered as inmate also the respondent No.2 company has not liable to pay the compensation as inmate is not covered as a third party.
Then the deceased loosed his control and fell down on the road, at that time the rear tyre of the tractor Trolley climbed over the deceased with result of it,
deceased sustained grievous injuries and died at hospital.
It clears that the deceased was neither coolie nor inmate of the tractor, he was third party.
When he came to Echi accident took place due to the negligence of driver.
Hence he is considered as third party and the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Tractor and Trailer and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount together with interest within two months from the date of this Siddayya N Alias Nachukkuri Siddayya vs Krishnareddy Alias Cheepathi ... on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131364038/

24. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988 is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,35,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 : 30%
 Petitioner No.2 : 70%
 Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
